headline: Structured Debate Activity With AI Devil's Advocate for ESL Classes
outcomes: Students construct and defend arguments in English against a challenging AI counterargument
Practise persuasion language — conceding, rebutting, building on evidence, signalling shifts
Develop the ability to argue a position they may not personally hold — a core academic skill
Build speaking confidence through structured debate where the format provides a clear scaffold
howItWorks: The AI generates a provocative statement about your topic — something students will genuinely disagree about
Students choose a side and submit their strongest argument for that position
The AI plays devil's advocate, challenging BOTH sides with targeted counterarguments
Students must respond to the AI's challenge — the exchange continues for 2–3 rounds of argument
teacherUseCases: Debate preparation — students practise the argument structure before a formal class debate
Academic writing foundation — building the skill of addressing counterarguments in essays
Critical thinking development — students must evaluate their own position under intellectual pressure

faq.q: What makes the AI's counterarguments effective?
faq.a: The AI is instructed to generate genuine challenges — not strawmen. It identifies the weakest assumption in each argument and targets that specifically, which pushes students to think more carefully about their reasoning.

faq.q: Can students change sides after seeing the counterarguments?
faq.a: Yes — the teacher can open a 'flip' phase where students who've been persuaded can switch sides and explain why. This is one of the most productive moments in the activity.

Topics with genuinely two-sided arguments work best — social media, technology, education policy, environmental trade-offs. The AI generates the statement, so you can also just set a broad topic and let it find the provocative angle.

faq.q: How do students submit their arguments?
faq.a: Students type their arguments on their phone or tablet through a browser. No app or student account needed — they join via the teacher's session link.

faq.q: What proficiency level works best for debate?
faq.a: Hot Take Arena works best from B1 upward. The AI can simplify counterarguments and vocabulary at lower difficulty settings. Below B1, the teacher should provide sentence starters and vocabulary support.

faq.q: Does Hot Take Arena require a subscription?
faq.a: Hot Take Arena is free to run. Students join via a browser link — no paid plan or student account required.
